title: Chaldean Catholic book states and earlier East Syriac anaphoral witnesses

traditions.label: Earlier Church of the East manuscript witnesses
traditions.scope: Shared ancestral anaphoral witnesses; not projected as medieval Catholic books.
traditions.coverage_note: Written states and critical apparatus only; local variation and manuscript layers remain explicit.

traditions.label: Chaldean Catholic recension
traditions.scope: Chaldean Catholic native book line; Syro-Malabar is owned separately.
traditions.coverage_note: Bounded states in 1767, 1901, 2007, 2014 and 2020. The 1971 revision and early Catholic manuscripts remain acquisition gaps. The 2025 reprint is not counted as a revision.

sources.title: William F. Macomber, The Oldest Known Text of the Anaphora of the Apostles Addai and Mari, OCP 32 (1966), 335–371
sources.inspection: Page images inspected: pp. 335–357, 362–363, 366–367, 370–371; especially manuscript dates pp. 340–341, contents pp. 342–344, kushshaphe pp. 344–347, sigla pp. 354–357, post-Sanctus pp. 362–363, intercession pp. 366–367.
sources.limitations: Modern critical edition and collation, not direct inspection of the medieval codices. Its paleographic dates and qualified conclusions remain attributed. A complete acquired PDF does not mean a complete transcription.

sources.title: Eusèbe Renaudot, Liturgiarum orientalium collectio II (Paris, 1716), Liturgia beatorum Apostolorum, pp. 592–593 with note 16
sources.inspection: Google Books full-view page images of printed pp. 592–593 retrieved and read on 2026-10-21: p. 592 carries the Addai and Mari epiclesis and following prayers; p. 593 the consignation and fraction, with note 16 and two marginal notes on the dominical words.
sources.limitations: Renaudot's Latin translation and notes describe manuscripts he used; he does not give a shelfmark for Patriarch Joseph's 1697 copy, and his phrase 'Missale Chaldaicum Romae editum' does not identify which Roman printing he meant. The manuscript itself was not inspected.

sources.title: Missale Chaldaicum ex decreto Sacrae Congregationis de Propaganda Fide editum (Rome, 1767), Google-origin original scan
sources.inspection: Complete 634-page PDF retained; original Latin and Syriac titles PDF 630–631 and Addai and Mari intercession printed p. 284/PDF 339 independently checked by two researchers. Related anaphora pages PDF 337–350 checked by one researcher. Source passages title and addai-mari-intercession bind exact hash 4d048b311c7f585e3824061d2d00727ad2e6e236f86ae6a876e4c36036348b5e.
sources.limitations: Bounded native-page collation of the intercession only. No complete liturgical transcription, full prayer inventory or comprehensive comparison of the 1767 and 1901 editions.

sources.title: Missale Chaldaicum ex decreto Sacrae Congregationis de Propaganda Fide editum (Rome, 1767), Russian State Library copy
sources.inspection: Catalogue title, Rome/Propaganda imprint, 1767 date, languages, extent [620] pages, complete-copy description, shelfmark ЗВ 10-8/10, and 2024 digitization information.
sources.limitations: Catalogue inspected; reader JavaScript did not expose a usable image/PDF acquisition path. Native book pages not independently inspected.

sources.title: HMML Reading Room: APSTCH EMAP07 00002, printed Missale Chaldaicum (1767)
sources.inspection: Record identifies 311 leaves, Rome 1767, title at f. 2r, text ff. 1v–310r, errata f. 310r, Syriac and Arabic/Garshuni.
sources.limitations: Images require registered access; no login or image inspection undertaken.

sources.title: Missale juxta ritum Ecclesiae Syrorum Orientalium, id est Chaldaeorum (Mosul, Dominican press, 1901)
sources.inspection: Retained full scan; images inspected at PDF 93–100, 102 and 77–78. Native opening printed pp. 4–7 = PDF 97–94, especially expanded Lord’s Prayer printed p. 5 = PDF 96; Latin imprimatur PDF 102 dated 22 October 1901. Anaphora beginning printed pp. 23–24 = PDF 78–77. Printed p. 35/PDF 67 was independently compared with Rome 1767 p. 284/PDF 339 on 2026-10-17; the life-giving Gospel phrase is present.
sources.limitations: Full book not transcribed or collated. The intercession phrase is directly page-collated; the institution-narrative comparison remains supported by the critical edition.

sources.title: Proprium missarum de tempore et de sanctis juxta ritum Ecclesiae Syrorum Orientalium, id est Chaldaeorum (Mosul, 1901)
sources.inspection: Bonn title/imprint and 310-page proper-volume identity; existing repository record and registered complete scan checked.
sources.limitations: Complementary temporal/sanctoral volume, not a successive recension. Proper texts and calendar changes not independently collated in this lane.

sources.title: Bishop Sarhad Yawsip Jammo, The Chaldean Liturgical Reform: Time Ripe for Implementation (5 December 2006; mirrored 28 December)
sources.inspection: Full article read from acquired HTML, especially Acts of the Holy Synod, Recognitio of the Holy See, and Final Decision of the Holy Synod.
sources.limitations: Firsthand committee-member account on a secondary mirror of kaldu.org. The original 2006 letter and Najm Al-Mashriq statement are cited by the author but were not independently acquired. Later Sako account disputes the reception and conformity of the printed text.

sources.title: Mar Awa Royel, The Pearl of Great Price: The Anaphora of the Apostles Mar Addai & Mar Mari as an Ecclesial and Cultural Identifier of the Assyrian Church of the East, OCP 80 (2014), 5–22
sources.inspection: PDF printed pp. 20–21, notes 48 and 50, image inspected; title/publication metadata also read.
sources.limitations: An Assyrian hierarch’s scholarly assessment of the Chaldean reform, with explicit criticism. Descriptive change claims are attributed; his theological evaluation is not adopted. Not a Catholic promulgation act.

sources.title: Liturgia sanctorum Apostolorum Adaei et Maris, cui accedunt duae aliae ... necnon ordo baptismi (Urmia: typis Missionis Archiepiscopi Cantuariensis, 1890), ULB Bonn scan
sources.inspection: Retained research scan (sha256 7ce986c3…f5b8): PDF 174 viewed on 2026-10-21. It carries a Latin title, the Syriac title in black and red, Syriac imprint lines and the Latin imprint 'Urmiae. Typis Missionis Archiepiscopi Cantuariensis. MDCCCXC'. Its Syriac title and imprint setting was compared line by line with the title photograph published by Patriarch Sako on 27 August 2025; the photograph shows no Latin title or Latin imprint (cropped, covered by the caption, or a Syriac-only issue), so the match rests on the identical Syriac setting.
sources.limitations: Collateral Anglican mission edition for the Church of the East (Macomber's Ur), not a Catholic book. Only the title leaf was compared here; the Syriac imprint lines were matched as a setting, not transcribed.

sources.title: رتبة القداس بحسب الطقس الكلداني / The Order of the Mass: The Liturgy of the Blessed Apostles (Baghdad, 2014)
sources.inspection: Title and page images pp. 1–8 and 25 inspected; original Italian recognitio p. 2, Arabic version p. 3, Sako preface p. 4 dated 27 October 2014, rubrics pp. 5–6, Syriac/Arabic beginning p. 8, anaphoral memorial and epiclesis p. 25.
sources.limitations: Institutional CMSIndia copy (RR 065). Despite English title, the body inspected is Syriac/Arabic. Not an independent English translation stage. Modern copyrighted text: metadata and bounded analysis only.

sources.title: رُتَب القداس بحسب الطقس الكلداني / Chaldean Catholic Missal (Baghdad, 2020), born-digital PDF hosted by a Chaldean parish
sources.inspection: Retained research copy (167 PDF pages, sha256 c14144d8…cb74, Word-generated 12 March 2020). PDF 1 title, PDF 2 decree, PDF 3 introduction and instructions 1–4, PDF 4 instructions 4–15 and note viewed as page images on 2026-10-21; earlier lane read section titles at PDF 5, 49, 87, 111 and 153.
sources.limitations: Born-digital file of the 2020 collection, not a scan of the printed impression; printed pagination may differ. Modern protected text: bounded analysis only. Only the listed pages were viewed in this lane.

sources.title: Patriarch Louis Raphaël Sako, decree No. 31 promulgating the typical edition of the Chaldean Taksa, Baghdad, 17 February 2020
sources.inspection: Signed and sealed Arabic and English decree reproduced as an image at PDF 2 of the 2020 digital edition, viewed on 2026-10-21: synod study in 2014, 2016 and 2019; unanimous approval at the synod of 3–11 August 2019 of the Addai and Mari orders, the second anaphora and the new Mass of Thomas; recognition by letter of the Congregation for the Oriental Churches dated 21 November 2019; typical edition in Syriac, Arabic and the spoken Chaldean dialect effective 5 April 2020.
sources.limitations: Reproduction inside a parish-hosted digital book, not an archival original. The Congregation's letter itself is unseen; Sako (2025) gives 20 November 2019 against the decree's 21 November.

sources.title: Congregatio pro Ecclesiis Orientalibus, Prot. N. 57/2003, recognitio ad quinquennium, 20 October 2014
sources.inspection: Original Italian letter reproduced on book p. 2, signature block Sandri/Vasil, date 20 October 2014; Arabic translation p. 3.
sources.limitations: Recognitio of proposed modifications for five years, not a claim that every parish implemented the same text or that trial expiry itself created a new recension.

sources.title: Louis Raphaël Sako, القداس الأول لأدّاي وماري: الأصالة والتجديد (27 August 2025)
sources.inspection: Full article read, particularly طبعات الرتبة; تجديد2005; تجديد2014–2020; and صلاة التقدمة.
sources.limitations: Participant retrospective, not the original synodal minutes. Some historical dates are typographically suspect; do not use its early-origin assertions to date manuscript composition. Its precise 20 November 2019 confirmation differs from the looser 2020 wording in the November 2025 reprint notice.

sources.title: Chaldean Patriarchate, سؤال وجواب عن تلاوة أبانا الذي في القداس (10 August 2025)
sources.inspection: Question and answer paragraphs concerning beginning/end repetitions and the synodal decisions 2014–2019.
sources.limitations: Reports a reform interval, not a precise individual decree date. Its attribution of the expanded prayer to Timothy I is not used as a separately established eighth-century book stage.

sources.title: رُتب القداس بحسب الطقس الكلداني / Chaldean Catholic Missal (Baghdad, 2025 reprint)
sources.inspection: Title PDF 3; preface/rubrics printed iii–iv (PDF 5–6); Sunday order title PDF 7; preparation printed 3 (PDF 9); intercessions/anamnesis/epiclesis printed 24–27 (PDF 30–33); Thomas opening printed 81 (PDF 87); contents PDF 173.
sources.limitations: Complete 176-page PDF acquired temporarily; only listed pages inspected. Reprint of 2020 collection according to publisher, with typographic/linguistic corrections. It cannot by itself prove every 2025 wording was present in 2020. No protected full-text import.

sources.title: Chaldean Patriarchate, إعادة طبع رُتَب القدّاس بحسب الطقس الكلداني (9 November 2025)
sources.inspection: Full notice read: exhausted 2020 missal and 2023 faithful’s book, reprinting after typographic/linguistic correction, 2014–2020 synodal study, confirmation and uniform use.
sources.limitations: Not an independent substantive reform. Permission for overseas parishes to print for use is not a general repository redistribution licence. Confirmation year stated broadly as 2020; original act still needed.

stages.label: Mar Eshaya: anaphora without written private prayers
stages.scope: Original anaphoral portion of a Hudra that also preserves Theodore and Nestorius; not a reconstructed complete missal.
stages.witness_label: Mosul, Mar Eshaya Hudra, Apostles anaphora manuscript pp. 463–466
stages.summary: Addai and Mari is written without the kushshaphe and without an institution narrative. The Hudra places Theodore at Christmas, Nestorius at Epiphany, and the Apostles after Easter baptism.

evidence.claim: Paleographic date, arrangement and edited Syriac anaphora distinguish the original portion from thirteenth-century additions.

stages.limitations: The date is approximate; later additions cannot be backdated. Absence from a Hudra does not alone prove a prayer was never said. No second/third-century composition date inferred.
stages.reception: Church of the East manuscript heritage; no claim of medieval Chaldean Catholic reception.

stages.label: Diarbekir: private prayers written with the anaphora
stages.scope: Apostles anaphora in one volume of a formerly three-volume Hudra.
stages.witness_label: Diarbekir Hudra, surviving second volume, Macomber siglum A
stages.summary: This witness includes the private celebrant prayers normally preceding the ghanta, unlike the Mar Eshaya text.

evidence.claim: Identifies and dates the witness and explicitly reports its kushshaphe.

stages.limitations: The surviving volume covers entry into Lent to the end of Easter week. Missing Christmas/Epiphany sections are a volume-survival issue, not suppression of their anaphoras. No universal introduction date established.
stages.reception: Historical Church of the East witness; modern Catholic ownership/location would not establish original Catholic use.

stages.label: Mardin 22: older form still written without private prayers
stages.scope: Anaphoral text within a surviving second Hudra volume.
stages.summary: The kushshaphe are absent in this dated later witness, showing that manuscript forms cannot be arranged as a simple universal progression.

evidence.claim: Date 1287 and omission; possible older exemplar or local nonrecognition discussed.

stages.limitations: Macomber treats abbreviated Hudra copying and local nonrecognition as alternatives requiring care. This does not establish a 1287 reform removing prayers.
stages.reception: Church of the East heritage, not evidence that the Catholic recension existed in 1287.

stages.label: Rome: Patriarch Joseph's manuscript with reformed dominical-words locus
stages.scope: One Catholic East Syriac manuscript state of the Apostles' anaphora, known only through Renaudot's note at the consignation and fraction.
stages.witness_label: Manuscript written at Rome in 1697 by Joseph, Chaldean patriarch, as described by Renaudot (1716); shelfmark not given
stages.summary: Renaudot's base codex (the codex of Elias) lacks the whole recitation of Christ's words at the consignation before the fraction. He reports that in the copy Patriarch Joseph wrote at Rome in 1697 that entire locus was reformed after the Missale Chaldaicum printed at Rome, as in the Mass whose version Alexis de Menezes published; a marginal note places a prayer after the dominical words in a more recent codex.

evidence.locus: Vol. II p. 593 note 16 and marginal notes; context p. 592
evidence.claim: Describes the omission in the codex of Elias and the 1697 Rome copy's reform of the locus after the Roman-printed Chaldean missal.

stages.limitations: Known only from Renaudot's description; the manuscript, its exact wording and shelfmark are unidentified. Which Roman printing Renaudot meant (before 1716; possibly the Maronite 'Missale Chaldaicum' of 1592/1594) is not established. No continuity with the 1767 Propaganda edition is asserted.
stages.reception: A copy by the Catholic patriarch at Rome attests a Catholic editorial state; local use of the copy is not established.

stages.label: Rome: Catholic Propaganda missal recension
stages.scope: Catholic printed witness; bounded Addai and Mari readings established through the critical apparatus, full ordinary not yet inspected.
stages.witness_label: Missale Chaldaicum ex decreto Sacrae Congregationis de Propaganda Fide editum (Rome, 1767)
stages.summary: The original Propaganda title identifies a Catholic printed state. In the Addai and Mari intercession, printed p. 284 omits the life-giving Gospel phrase that the Mosul 1901 printed p. 35 includes.

evidence.locus: Title PDF 630; Addai and Mari printed p. 284/PDF 339
evidence.claim: Original title and bounded native intercession directly checked; omitted phrase independently confirmed.
Identifies the complete 1767 Catholic Propaganda edition.

evidence.locus: p. 357 siglum Cr; p. 366 line 53 apparatus; p. 345 note 2
evidence.claim: Identifies Cr as 1767 pp. 280–286 and distinguishes the older printed omission from the later Mosul reading.

stages.limitations: Only the titles and selected anaphoral pages have been checked. No claim of first Catholic printing or complete list of Latin/Maronite additions. Institution placement at the fraction still requires a precise comparison.
stages.reception: Publication by the Roman Propaganda Congregation identifies a Catholic book; breadth and continuity of local adoption not independently established.

stages.label: Mosul: ordinary and complementary propers
stages.scope: One publication state represented by complementary ordinary/anaphoral and temporal-sanctoral proper volumes.
stages.witness_label: Missale juxta ritum Ecclesiae Syrorum Orientalium, id est Chaldaeorum; companion Proprium missarum de tempore et de sanctis (Mosul, Dominican press, 1901)
stages.summary: The ordinary prints the expanded Lord’s Prayer near the beginning and the life-giving Gospel phrase in the Addai and Mari intercession. Macomber locates the institution narrative at the opening of the post-Sanctus prayer.

evidence.claim: Native beginning and 1901 imprimatur inspected.
Complementary proper volume shares the 1901 Mosul Dominican imprint.

evidence.locus: p. 357 Cm 01; p. 363 note 10; p. 366 line 53 apparatus
evidence.claim: Specifies 1901 pp. 24–36 as Cm 01 and records the relevant anaphoral readings.
Native intercession directly checked against Rome 1767 printed p. 284/PDF 339.

stages.limitations: The companion volume is not a second stage. 1901 attests these readings; it does not date their introduction. Macomber also finds the post-Sanctus insertion in a late nineteenth-century Mar Ya‘qob ritual.
stages.reception: Catholic imprimatur from Henricus Altmayer, Apostolic Delegate, 22 October 1901. It authorizes printing; it does not establish universal use or an independent complete reform.

stages.label: Reformed Taksa associated with Jammo
stages.scope: Identifiable reform described by its compiler and scholarly observer; text identity and reception distinguished.
stages.witness_label: Reformed Takhsa d-Raze, approved 2005/recognized 2006 according to Jammo; original Syriac edition still to acquire
stages.summary: The reform places the institution narrative after the intercessions, before the epiclesis/anamnesis sequence, and directs audible anaphoral recitation. Royel also describes removal of diaconal exhortations around the Pax.

evidence.claim: Reports 2005 synod, 18 February 2006 recognitio, and 6 January 2007 implementation date.
Describes rearrangement, litanies and audible recitation.
Sako disputes broad reception of the printed reform and whether it incorporated the synod’s corrections.

stages.limitations: No original Syriac 2007 edition acquired. Two Internet Archive English aids were found; neither is silently substituted for a native text. The effective date is the reported synodal decision, not proof of universal implementation.
stages.reception: Jammo states St Peter’s diocese would implement. Sako later disputes wider acceptance and whether the printed text included synodal corrections; these accounts are not collapsed into universal reception.

stages.label: Baghdad: five-year trial order of the Apostles
stages.scope: Printed Addai and Mari order with official letter, patriarchal introduction and new practical rubrics.
stages.witness_label: رتبة القداس بحسب الطقس الكلداني / The Order of the Mass: The Liturgy of the Blessed Apostles (Baghdad, 2014), Syriac/Arabic
stages.summary: The native opening omits the expanded Lord’s Prayer; its Gloria and conditional psalmody lead to the opening prayer. Rubrics require audible prayer and distinguish the priest’s initial orientation from the offertory facing the people.

evidence.claim: Title, opening and rubrics image checked.
The Congregation exceptionally grants the proposed modifications recognitio ad quinquennium on 20 October 2014.

stages.limitations: The 35-page institutional PDF is not a full annual missal set. No complete transcription. Its 2015 PDF metadata does not replace the 2014 book date.
stages.reception: Patriarchal preface 27 October 2014 presents the trial order for the Chaldean Church. Authoritative direction and actual parish compliance remain distinct.

stages.label: Baghdad: revised collection with new Thomas order
stages.date_label: 2020 typical edition; decree No. 31 of 17 February 2020, effective 5 April 2020
stages.scope: Collection of Sunday/feast and weekday Apostles orders, Thomas order, and second anaphora; 2025 reprint used only as a later witness.
stages.witness_label: رُتب القداس بحسب الطقس الكلداني (Baghdad, 2020), witnessed by the official 2025 reprint Chaldean Catholic Missal
stages.summary: The collection incorporates a newly composed order named for Thomas alongside revised existing orders. The 2025 contents visibly separates Sunday/feast, weekday, Thomas, and second anaphora sections.

evidence.locus: تجديد2014–2020, paragraphs on the second anaphora and Thomas
evidence.claim: Reports revision of Theodore, new Thomas order reviewed in 2019, confirmation 20 November 2019 and 2020 publication.

evidence.locus: Contents PDF 173; Thomas printed p. 81/PDF 87; preface iii–iv
evidence.claim: Confirms contents and native Syriac/Arabic presentation of the later reprint.
Identifies 2025 as reprint of the exhausted 2020 collection.
Promulgates the typical edition in Syriac, Arabic and spoken Chaldean effective 5 April 2020, citing synods 2014–2019 and a recognition letter of 21 November 2019.

evidence.locus: PDF 1 title; PDF 3–4 introduction and instructions 1–15
evidence.claim: Title and celebration instructions of the 2020 collection read on the page images.

stages.limitations: Printed 2020 impression and the Holy See's letter not acquired; the 2020 text is read from a born-digital copy. Sako gives the confirmation as 20 November 2019, the decree 21 November 2019, and the November 2025 notice loosely 2020. The 2025 reprint's instructions (printed iii–iv) differ in detail from 2020 PDF 3–4: an entrance-chant alternative noting the absence of a sanctuary curtain, an added alternative epiclesis chant, sixteen numbered items instead of fifteen, and an introduction no longer naming Sureth and English. These are recorded as reprint corrections, not a separately approved revision.
stages.reception: Official patriarchal collection; publisher prescribes common use. Actual use in every eparchy is not established by publication. Arabic/Sureth/English translation histories remain separate.

transitions.summary: The later Hudra writes private celebrant prayers absent from the earlier witness.

changes.before: Kushshaphe not written in the Mar Eshaya anaphora.
changes.after: Kushshaphe are written in the twelfth-century Diarbekir Hudra.

evidence.claim: Explicit comparison of the witnesses and caution about oral use versus written absence.
Source describes the difference and competing explanations.

transitions.limitations: This is a witnessed textual difference, not a demonstrated direct revision or universal introduction. Mardin 22 (1287) continues to lack the prayers; no linear chronology of adoption is implied.

transitions.summary: The Mosul intercession contains the life-giving Gospel phrase omitted in the Roman 1767 reading.

changes.before: The phrase ܒܐܘܢܓܠܝܘܢܗ ܡܚܝܢܐ (in his life-giving Gospel) is absent from the intercession.
changes.after: The intercession includes ܒܐܘܢܓܠܝܘܢܗ ܡܚܝܢܐ (in his life-giving Gospel).
changes.locus_before: Rome 1767 Addai and Mari, printed p. 284/PDF 339, right column bottom continuing at left column top
changes.locus_after: Mosul 1901 Addai and Mari, printed p. 35/PDF 67, upper half

evidence.claim: Original intercession passes from what the Lord and God taught to purity/holiness without the phrase.
Original intercession contains the life-giving Gospel phrase at the corresponding locus.

evidence.locus: p. 345 note 2; p. 366 line 53; p. 357 sigla
evidence.claim: Cr is included among omissions; Cm is not. Author explains that recent Chaldean editions preserve the older reading here.
Original intercession passes from what the Lord and God taught to purity/holiness without the phrase.
Original intercession contains the life-giving Gospel phrase at the corresponding locus.
Bounded intercession variant, not a complete edition collation.

transitions.limitations: The original pages establish this one variant between the two printed witnesses. Exact introduction date and direct 1767-to-1901 editorial dependence are unproved. The bounded phrase is not a complete prayer or book transcription.

transitions.summary: The institution narrative moves from the opening post-Sanctus position to after the intercessions.

changes.before: Institution narrative inserted after the opening thanks of the post-Sanctus prayer.
changes.after: Narrative placed after the intercessions, immediately before the epiclesis/anamnesis sequence described by Royel.
changes.locus_after: Reformed anaphora described in Royel p. 20 note 48

evidence.claim: Locates the Mosul insertion.
Locates the reformed insertion after the intercessions.
Identifies the reform’s approval and announced implementation chronology.

transitions.limitations: No full native 2007 book collated. Intermediate 1936/1971 states remain uncollated; this comparison does not assert that every change occurred at once or that 2007 replaced 1901 everywhere.

transitions.summary: The 2014 Syriac opening omits the expanded Lord’s Prayer printed after the Gloria in 1901.

changes.before: Gloria followed by the expanded Abun d-bashmayya, including the triple Holy interpolation and doxological repetition.
changes.after: The opening sequence, including a printed provision for Psalm 35, reaches Peace be with us and the opening prayer without the expanded Abun sequence.

evidence.claim: Opening sequence read on the native page images.
Native opening read on the page image.

evidence.locus: Question and answer on beginning/end repetitions
evidence.claim: Official explanation dates the synodal deletion process to 2014–2019 and retains the pre-Communion position.

transitions.limitations: This is a bounded comparison of two native openings, not full-book collation or proof of direct descent. Later official account supplies reform context. The closing deletion and retained Communion prayer were source-described, not independently collated here. No claim that deletion first occurred everywhere on the book’s publication date.

transitions.summary: The Apostles trial order is followed by a collection that revises Theodore and adds a newly composed Thomas order.

changes.before: The identified 2014 trial book contains the Apostles order.
changes.after: The subsequent collection includes a revised second anaphora and new Thomas order.
changes.locus_after: 2020 collection described by Sako; 2025 reprint contents and Thomas p. 81

evidence.claim: Identifies the Apostles order.
Author describes the new Thomas composition and work on Theodore.
Later printed witness has separate Thomas and second-anaphora sections.

changes.before: Apostles order presented as one trial booklet.
changes.after: Sunday/feast and weekday orders are printed as separate sections of the collection.

evidence.claim: Identifies the scope of the earlier book.
Separates Sunday and weekday sections.
Describes collection development and 2020 printing.
Identifies the later book as reprint of 2020.

transitions.limitations: Evidence level applies to substantive original reform as described by its author; no complete 2014/2020 native-text collation. Do not treat Theodore’s absence from the 2014 Apostles booklet as its abolition, nor the new Thomas title as ancient apostolic authorship. Arabic wording changes alone are not native Syriac changes.

transitions.summary: The 2020 celebration instructions assign the new repertoire, allow a choice of Creed, move the final blessing to the altar and change the Communion provision.

changes.before: The 21 numbered instructions of the trial booklet address the single Apostles order and contain no provision for choosing a form of the Creed.
changes.after: Instruction 6 allows either the Apostles' Creed or the Nicene–Constantinopolitan Creed, as decided by the 2019 synod.

evidence.claim: 2014 celebration instructions read on the page images.
2020 celebration instructions read on the page images.

changes.before: Instruction 18: one concluding prayer, then the final blessing, and the procession leaves after the announcements.
changes.after: Instruction 15: the final blessing is given from the altar, not from the middle of the sanctuary, as decided by the 2019 synod; the procession then leaves during the closing chant.

evidence.claim: 2014 celebration instructions read on the page images.
2020 celebration instructions read on the page images.

changes.before: Instruction 17: Communion in the hand, left over right, and under both kinds when communicants are few.
changes.after: Instruction 14: Communion in the mouth or in the hand at the communicant's choice, with the words Body of Christ and the answer Amen; no both-kinds provision appears in the list.

evidence.claim: 2014 celebration instructions read on the page images.
2020 celebration instructions read on the page images.

changes.before: The instructions presuppose the one Apostles order printed in the booklet.
changes.after: Instruction 1 prescribes the Apostles or Mar Thoma order on Sundays and feasts, the weekday Apostles order or Mar Thoma on ordinary days, and the second anaphora on great feasts.

evidence.claim: 2014 celebration instructions read on the page images.
2020 celebration instructions read on the page images.
2014 celebration instructions read on the page images.
2020 celebration instructions read on the page images.
Places the 2020 texts after synodal study in 2014, 2016 and 2019.

transitions.limitations: Comparison of the two instruction lists only, not of the prayer texts. An instruction absent from a list does not prove the practice was forbidden or that the book lacked a corresponding text elsewhere. The 2020 text is a born-digital copy, not the printed impression.

gaps.missing: Direct manuscript images and current repository identifiers for Mar Eshaya, Diarbekir Hudra and Mardin 22; precise layer separation.
gaps.next_source: Macomber 1966 pp. 340–354; Centre numérique des manuscrits orientaux/Ankawa and HMML catalogues. Sako 2025 reports an electronic Mar Eshaya copy from the Ankawa manuscript centre.
gaps.consequence: Critical-edition evidence establishes bounded written states; no manuscript-level transcription or complete stemma is claimed.

gaps.missing: Catholic manuscript revisions before 1767 beyond Renaudot's description: the identity, shelfmark and wording of Patriarch Joseph's 1697 Rome copy, which Roman printing it followed, and the original 1767 institution/fraction pages. Renaudot II p. 593 n. 16 is now read and recorded as a stage.
gaps.next_source: Vatican Syriac manuscripts of the Chaldean group labelled by Macomber (Vat. sir. 491 of 1686, 44 of 1691, 43 of 1701) and any Vatican or Propaganda copy dated 1697 by Patriarch Joseph I; Russian State Library ЗВ 10-8/10 complete 1767 digitization; HMML APSTCH EMAP07 00002.
gaps.consequence: No invented 1552/1697 complete-missal stage; Catholic reception and institution-placement claims await direct or critical verification.

gaps.missing: Complete 1767/1901 native-body collation, especially where (if anywhere) 1767 prints the institution narrative and the fraction arrangement, and borrowed prayers.
